figures.photoQuote: Walk through the front door of the house Dad built.

_feed_howto: ONE woven stream of stills and clips, shown in this order. Photo item:  { "type":"photo", "src":"land-1.jpg", "caption":"optional line" }. Clip item:   { "type":"video", "id":"YOUTUBE_ID", "title":"Warehouse keys", "caption":"optional", "date":"Jun 2026" }. To intersperse a clip, just drop a video item between two photo items. id = the bit after watch?v= / youtu.be/ / shorts/. Unlisted is fine.

feed.title: the LAND — trailer
feed.caption: Start here: a door in London that opens onto seven acres in Grenada.

feed.title: Journey to Grenada
feed.caption: Episode 1 — the flight down, the last mile past the Welcome-to-Paradise sign, and the first sight of the seven acres.

feed.title: The Building
feed.caption: Episode 2 — the house Dad built, the warehouse behind it, and what each structure could still become.

feed.title: Grenada History
feed.caption: Episode 3 — the island's story in full, from the first peoples through colonisation to independence.

feed.title: Grenada History — 10 Things
feed.caption: Episode 3a — a second pass through the island's story, told in ten turns.

feed.title: The Locality
feed.caption: Episode 4 — Simon, St Andrew: the road, the neighbours, the bay below.

feed.title: Inside the House — the vote
feed.caption: Episode 5 — four ways to bring the house back. You get a vote.

feed.title: Option A
feed.caption: Episode 5a — a walk through Option A, room by room.

feed.title: Stone, Timber, Water
feed.caption: Episode 6 — the old mill, the warehouse, and a river found at the far edge of the seven acres.

feed.title: No Small Undertaking
feed.caption: Episode 7 — reckoning with the size of it: what it really takes to bring a place back.

feed.title: The Homecoming
feed.caption: Episode 8 — the whole country throws its arms open and calls its children home. I went — and found the whole island asking my question.

feed.title: The Business of Coming Home
feed.caption: Episode 9 — the morning after, the same hall becomes a business forum. Belonging, or a balance sheet?

feed.title: Two Grenadas
feed.caption: Episode 10 — the Grenada on the postcards against the one that's just lived in. The one being sold, and the one being kept.

feed.title: The First Wash
feed.caption: Episode 11 — the house my parents built, thirty years in the weather. Not an architect, not a plan the size of a building — a Saturday, a pressure washer, and a man willing to climb up onto the roof.
The house Dad built.
The barn, waiting.
The river boundary.
The bay below.

feed.title: The Northern Lime
feed.caption: Coconut Fest in Victoria, the Tivoli Drummers' Salaka — and, on a wall found by accident, the week the flag went up.

feed.title: Eleven Things About Food
feed.caption: The Spice Isle exported food for 300 years, and now imports its dinner. What it means to grow for ourselves.

feed.title: Eleven Things About Health
feed.caption: The pharmacy, or the garden? Bush medicine, the nurse-export paradox, and growing the cure.

feed.title: Education in Grenada
feed.caption: Grown to leave, or grown to stay? The literacy revolution, the doctors it trains for the world, and coming home to teach.

feed.title: Work in Grenada
feed.caption: An economy that exports its people — a century of migrant labour, and the case for building livelihoods at home.

feed.title: Tourism in Grenada
feed.caption: Cruise ships that do not stay, a resort on a turtle beach, and tourism that could belong to Grenadians.
